problem: Serre's positivity conjecture that if R is a commutative regular local ring, and P, Q are prime ideals of R, then dim(R/P) + dim(R/Q) = dim(R) implies χ(R/P,R/Q) > 0
missing_details: P and Q must be prime ideals of R
dimensions refer to Krull dimension of the quotient rings
refined_question: Let R be a Noetherian, commutative, regular local ring and let P and Q be prime ideals of R such that the R-module (R/P)⊗_R(R/Q) has finite length. Define the intersection multiplicity χ(R/P,R/Q)=∑_{i=0}^∞(−1)^i·length_R(Tor_i^R(R/P,R/Q)). If dim(R/P)+dim(R/Q)=dim(R), is it true that χ(R/P,R/Q)>0?
justification: We consulted the Wikipedia article “Serre’s multiplicity conjectures” to extract the precise assumptions and statement of the positivity conjecture. The original name indicates positivity of an Euler‐characteristic‐defined intersection multiplicity but omits key hypotheses: regularity, Noetherian and local structure of R, finiteness of the tensor product, and the Tor‐based definition of χ. We have added all these to make the question fully self-contained and faithful to the canonical formulation.
